description: AGROVEGA is a team of passionate innovators driven by curiosity, creativity, and a shared ambition to solve real-world challenges. By combining technology, data science, and scientific thinking, we transform complex data into meaningful solutions. We believe in collaboration, innovation, and using space-based insights to build a smarter and more sustainable future for Earth.
summary: We built a web dashboard that turns live NASA POWER climate data into a ranked list of suitable crops for any location. Users pick one of 39 regions or enter GPS coordinates, and the app fetches recent temperature, humidity and rainfall from NASA POWER. It then scores seven crops (wheat, corn, tomato, potato, onion, barley, clover) so farmers can see what fits their local climate. It makes satellite data usable by non-experts and supports better crop and water planning.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

NASA Agro-Climatology is a web dashboard that turns NASA POWER climate data into a ranked list of suitable crops for any location. Users select one of 39 regions (Egyptian governorates and major farming areas worldwide) or enter custom GPS coordinates. The app then shows mean temperature, relative humidity and rainfall, and scores seven crops (wheat, corn, tomato, potato, onion, barley and clover) on a 0-100 suitability scale. Results appear in KPI cards, a daily time-series chart, a crop ranking chart, a radar chart of score components and a searchable table. Users can filter by season (summer/winter), import their own CSV or JSON data, and export results as CSV or JSON.

HOW IT WORKS

When the user presses "Sync live NASA data", the app calls the NASA POWER Daily API (AG community) directly from the browser for the selected coordinates, using the parameters T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M and PRECTOTCORR over the most recent ~25 days. Days with missing values are ignored. The app summarizes the data (mean temperature, mean relative humidity, total rainfall) and recomputes each crop's suitability score with a transparent weighted model: humidity 40%, temperature 35% (distance from a 25 C optimum), soil pH 15% (distance from 7.0) and crop priority 10%. The dashboard loads embedded sample data first; pressing Sync fetches live NASA POWER data, and the interface clearly labels whether the data shown is live or sample. If the NASA API cannot be reached, the app keeps the sample data and tells the user it is not live, rather than showing made-up values.

BENEFITS

- Makes satellite climate data easy to use for farmers and agricultural planners without technical training.

- Supports crop and irrigation planning with clear, comparable scores and short advice per crop.

- Works for any point on Earth, free to use, and runs entirely in the browser with no installation.

- Lets users bring their own data and export results for reports.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

Our goal is to help farmers choose crops that fit their local climate, reduce water waste and lower the risk of crop failure, using NASA's free and open data.

LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

The current model uses one shared temperature optimum for all crops, soil pH values are stored regional estimates (not satellite measurements), and humidity is air relative humidity (RH2M), not soil moisture. Planned improvements are crop-specific temperature and water thresholds, real soil moisture data (e.g. NASA SMAP), and a mobile-friendly offline mode.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Chart.js, Font Awesome, Google Fonts, NASA POWER REST API, GitHub Pages for hosting.
